note: Leaf blast favours long leaf-wetness at moderate temperature. docs/PRD.md section 6 uses this rule as the demo trigger. Tuned in Phase 3 (mean-in-band, 6 consecutive days) after the naive overlap test fired on 93% of farm-target pairs.
Associated with stressed and nutrient-poor crops, so the history bump matters more here than for blast.
Spreads on wind-driven rain; a short wet window is enough.
Dead-heart damage tracks crop age rather than the weather window.
Declares both drivers. Hopper burn needs a humid canopy AND a crop old enough to have one.

SOURCED (partial): TNAU (agritech.tnau.ac.in, cotton pest page 1) describes attack from 'early stages of square formation' through 'boll formation and maturation stage' -- larvae target shoots, buds, bracts and tender bolls throughout. No numeric weather band found; the phenology window is real but wide because the pest is polyphagous across most of the fruiting season.

SOURCED (partial): TNAU (cotton pest page 2) -- 'rosetted flowers', bore holes with excreta, 'attacked buds and immature bolls drop off' -- confirms the target attacks buds and immature bolls, i.e. the boll_formation window. This is the target the V2 brief named as needing boll_formation to exist; it now does (seed/growth_stages.py). No numeric weather band found for pink bollworm specifically.

EXCLUDED FROM SCORING. TNAU (cotton pest page, search-derived) gives symptom text (sap-sucking, sooty mould, LCV vector) but no days-after-sowing window or humidity/temperature band. Whitefly is broadly known to favour hot, dry weather, but I found no cited numeric band -- a rule invented to fill this entry would be the same defect as a dosage invented to fill a ladder rung. Real inspection tasks are still authored (seed/inspection_tasks.json); only the risk-alert rule is withheld.
EXCLUDED FROM SCORING. Same gap as whitefly: TNAU gives identification and damage symptoms, no sourced timing or weather band.

SOURCED: general plant-pathology literature on Xanthomonas citri pv. malvacearum (cross-referenced, Cotton Incorporated / NC State Extension pattern) -- RH above 85%, daytime 86-100F (30-38C), most severe after heavy rain or hail. Encoded as a moderate multi-day band rather than the literal storm trigger, since the risk engine scores daily weather rather than discrete rain events; consecutive_days set lower (5) than the fungal paddy diseases because bacterial spread is rain-splash driven and faster than fungal establishment.

EXCLUDED FROM SCORING. TNAU confirms whitefly transmits leaf curl virus, but I found no sourced numeric weather band or DAS window for the virus itself (as opposed to its vector, which is also UNSOURCED here -- see cotton_whitefly). Inventing a band by inference from an unsourced vector would compound one gap with another.

SOURCED (partial, phenology only): TNAU (agritech.tnau.ac.in/crop_protection/cotton_diseases/cotton_d1.html) -- symptoms 'typically first appear on lower leaves around the time of first flower', soil temperature 20-30C, favoured by 'hot and dry periods followed by rains', worse in heavy black soils (the dominant cotton soil in the Vidarbha/Marathwada belt). The dry-then-rain transition does not fit this engine's consecutive-favourable-days weather schema -- encoding it as a sustained humidity band would misrepresent the actual trigger (a rewetting stress event, not sustained wet weather), so only the flowering-stage phenology window is encoded and the weather half is left out rather than approximated.

SOURCED: field study (ResearchGate, 'Incidence of soybean stem fly during Rabi-summer') -- seedling mortality peaked 10-20 DAS, stem-tunnelling began by 30 DAS in Indian trial data. No numeric weather band found; the risk is age-driven, not weather-driven, which is consistent with the pest attacking the stem base of young plants.
EXCLUDED FROM SCORING. Symptom text is sourced (girdling cuts on stem, wilting, plant severed 15-25 cm above ground), but no days-after-sowing window or weather band was found.

EXCLUDED FROM SCORING. Covers green semilooper, tobacco caterpillar and chickpea caterpillar as a group, per the same grouping used in Indian Kharif soybean advisories. Sourced as a general Kharif-season, vegetative-through-pod-stage pest complex; no numeric band or precise DAS window found for the group.

SOURCED: field-correlation study (Indian Journal of Agricultural Research, 'Relationship between Whiteflies, Yellow Mosaic Severity, Weather and Crop Age in Soybean') -- disease progression correlates positively with evening relative humidity, negatively with maximum temperature and sunshine hours; spreads rapidly within the first two months of planting (approx. DAS 60). temp_max is set conservatively (30C) reflecting the negative correlation with high temperature, which is the opposite shape from the fungal paddy/cotton rules and is intentional.
EXCLUDED FROM SCORING. Colletotrichum truncatum symptom text is sourced (stem/pod/petiole lesions, premature defoliation), no numeric weather band found specific to Indian conditions.
EXCLUDED FROM SCORING. Symptom text sourced (leaf/pod/stem spots), no numeric band found.

SOURCED: cross-referenced US extension sources (Cornell CALS, UNL CropWatch, NC State) on Pseudomonas syringae pv. glycinea -- cool, wet weather (70-80F / 21-27C) favours development, disease stops in hot-dry conditions, rain-splash spread. Plant-pathogen temperature/humidity response is not geography-specific, so this is treated as usable for Indian Kharif conditions despite the sources being US-focused. temp_max set to 27C reflecting the documented 'stops in hot and dry conditions' ceiling -- this is a NARROWER band than the fungal rules, by design.

SOURCED: entomology literature (eagri.org / PMC, Atherigona soccata) -- 'attacks sorghum at 7-30 days after seedling emergence', deadheart symptom from maggot feeding in the central whorl. A precise, real, cited DAS window -- the strongest phenology source found in this pass.

EXCLUDED FROM SCORING. Chilo partellus symptom text is sourced (leaf scraping by young larvae, deadhearts, bore holes), and general entomology places it in the seedling-to-late-vegetative window, but no source gave a specific days-after-sowing range precise enough to encode without guessing at the boundary -- unlike shoot fly, where 7-30 DAS was explicit.

EXCLUDED FROM SCORING. Peregrinus maidis symptom text is sourced (sap-sucking, sooty mould, reddened midribs from egg-laying, stunting), including its role as a vector for sorghum stripe virus. No days-after-sowing window or weather band found.

EXCLUDED FROM SCORING. Colletotrichum sublineola symptom text is sourced (red leaf spots, black acervuli), no numeric weather band found -- the sources found covered resistance breeding, not epidemiology.

SOURCED, strongest band in this file: ICAR-IIMR (millets.res.in/pub/2020/Sorghum_grain_mold_2020.pdf) and ICRISAT (oar.icrisat.org) -- RH 95-98% and temperature 25-28C during the flowering-to-maturity window drive mold sporulation; AICRP-Sorghum hotspot testing locations for this disease include sites in Maharashtra. humidity_min set to 90 (slightly below the cited 95-98 peak) since this engine's daily-mean humidity reading will rarely hit the sporulation-chamber figure sustained for the full window; the phenology gate (flowering/grain_filling) is what actually narrows this rule.

EXCLUDED FROM SCORING, and not merely for lack of a source. Smut (grain replaced by sori) is a seed-borne systemic infection: the fungus infects at germination via contaminated seed and is only VISIBLE at panicle emergence. A current-weather risk alert cannot meaningfully warn about an infection that was already determined at sowing -- this is a wrong-shaped rule, not an unsourced one. Inspection tasks are still authored so a farmer knows what to look for at grain-fill/maturity.

SOURCED: Peronosclerospora sorghi literature (eagri.org / oar.icrisat.org) -- RH near 100%, temperature 21-23C, light drizzling and cool weather at the seedling / 3-4-leaf stage produce systemic infection with chlorotic downy growth. humidity_min set to 95 rather than the cited ~100 for the same daily-mean-reading reason as grain mold; consecutive_days lower (4) since the seedling-stage infection window is itself short.
